facts.statement: The Cuban giant owl was an extinct genus of owls that stood 1.1 meters tall.
facts.quote: The Cuban giant owl or cursorial giant owl (Ornimegalonyx) is an extinct genus of giant owl that measured 1.1 m in height.

facts.statement: Remains of the animal have been found in cave deposits dating from 126,000 to 11,700 years ago.
facts.quote: Remains have been found in cave deposits from the Late Pleistocene period (126,000 to 11,700 years ago).

facts.statement: The animal lived on the island of Cuba.
facts.quote: It lived on the island of Cuba.

facts.statement: The first fossil specimen was initially mistaken for a member of the family Phorusrhacidae because its bones were so large.
facts.quote: The first fossil specimen was mistakenly described as a bird in the family Phorusrhacidae, in part because the bones were so large.

facts.statement: In 1961, Pierce Brodkorb correctly identified the fossils as belonging to an owl.
facts.quote: In 1961, Pierce Brodkorb reviewed the findings and identified them to have belonged to an owl.

facts.statement: A 2020 study concluded that previously described species were synonyms of O. oteroi and described a new valid species, O. ewingi, from material once assigned to Bubo osvaldoi.
facts.quote: A 2020 study concluded that those species are all synonyms of O. oteroi, and describe a new valid species, Ornimegalonyx ewingi, from material formerly assigned to the prehistoric horned owl Bubo osvaldoi.

facts.statement: Arredondo estimated the height of the animal to be 1.1 meters.
facts.quote: Arredondo estimated the height of Ornimegalonyx to have been 1.1 m tall.

facts.statement: While initially estimated at 30 kg, later studies suggest the animal's body mass was between 9 and 13.5 kg.
facts.quote: Its body mass in life is initially estimated to have been approximately 30 kg, but later studies suggest a mass of 9 to 13.5 kg.

facts.statement: The animal had very large and powerfully built legs and feet.
facts.quote: The legs and feet of the Cuban giant owl appear to be very large and powerfully built.

facts.statement: The animal had a reduced keel on its sternum, suggesting it may have been capable of short bursts of flight.
facts.quote: The keel of the sternum was reduced and the owl may have been capable of short burst of flight.

facts.statement: It is probable that the animal only flew when extremely pressed, preferring to run like a modern wild turkey.
facts.quote: It is probable that, like a modern wild turkey, the owl only took flight when extremely pressed, more often choosing to run.

facts.statement: Females of this species were larger than males.
facts.quote: The females of this owl species were larger than the males.

facts.statement: It was probably an ambush predator that pounced on unsuspecting prey with its crushing talons.
facts.quote: It was probably an ambush predator that would pounce on unsuspecting prey with its crushing talons.

facts.statement: The animal belongs to the class Aves, order Strigiformes, and family Strigidae.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Aves ordo: Strigiformes familia: Strigidae genus: Ornimegalonyx †

facts.statement: The type species is O. oteroi, described by Arredondo in 1954, while O. minor, O. gigas, and O. acevedoi were described by Arredondo in 1982.
facts.quote: subdivision: O. oteroi Arredondo, 1954 (especie tipo) O. minor Arredondo, 1982 O. gigas Arredondo, 1982 O. acevedoi Arredondo, 1982

facts.statement: When the first specimen was described in the 1950s, its large bones led to it being classified as a member of the family Phorusrhacidae.
facts.quote: Cuando se describió el primer espécimen en la década de 1950, los huesos eran tan grandes que se describieron como pertenecientes a un ave de la familia Phorusrhacidae.

facts.statement: Remains are found abundantly across the island in Late Pleistocene cave deposits, with at least three nearly complete skeletons discovered.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encuentran abundantemente a lo largo de la isla, en depósitos de cuevas desde el periodo Pleistoceno tardío (de hace unos 10000 años) y se han encontrado por lo menos tres esqueletos casi completos.

facts.statement: It is believed the owl was at least 1 meter tall and likely weighed over 9 kg.
facts.quote: Se cree que este búho tenía por lo menos 1m de alto y probablemente su peso excedía fácilmente los 9kg.

facts.statement: The reduced keel on the sternum suggests the owl may have been capable of short, sudden flights.
facts.quote: La quilla del esternón estaba reducida (si estuviera ausente habría sido imposible que volara) y este búho pudo haber sido capaz de cortos vuelos súbitos.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the animal may have been capable of killing prey weighing 35 kg or more.
facts.quote: Esto sugiere que Ornimegalonyx pudo haber matado presas de 35kg o más.

facts.statement: It is believed the animal primarily preyed on large rodents like Heteropsomys and Macrocapromys, as well as medium-sized mammals such as ground sloths.
facts.quote: Se cree que el búho corredor gigante capturara principalmente presas de grandes roedores, incluyendo a Heteropsomys, Capromys, Geocapromys y Macrocapromys (del tamaño de un moderno capibara o carpincho) y otros mamíferos de tamaño medio, como los perezosos terrestres, tales como Cubanocnus, Miocnus, Mesocnus y Megalocnus.

facts.statement: The time range of the genus spans from the Gelasian to the Holocene, approximately 2.58 to 0 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Gelasian to Holocene (2.58 to 0 million years ago)
